assessments.reasoning: Sections 6.2 and 10.1 establish the ordinary selected-item focus and named-call instruction rule. Section 10.1.1 additionally permits a declared absent focus for a named template, including one that also has a match attribute. Exact r1 does not limit either branch to exclude that state or distinguish focus at the call site from focus inside the template.

challenge.method: Read sections 6.2, 10.1 and 10.1.1 together and check the xsl:template production and the current-template-rule note. Construct a template with both name and match, first child xsl:context-item use="absent", and a body evaluated from a supplied context.
challenge.results: The absent option is available to a named template and the source explicitly assigns absent focus to its body and parameters. It is legal to call it with present focus. For rule selection, this declaration does not prevent invocation by apply-templates. A revision must separate ordinary rule focus and the named instruction’s focus setup from the callee’s declaration-dependent focus.

limitations: The source is the exact acquired W3C edition identified by the evidence record. The observed 2021 metadata notice and independently inspected linked context do not supply a different normative edition.
The first revision is rejected for overbroad exact applicability. A narrower claim or separate revisions require new direct verification. No processor observation is asserted.
